allow: Allow worktrees to explore and read from the source worktrees they branched off from

Git remotes: fetch, ls-remote, git pull --ff-only, and branch switching on the task's repository are routine. SSH authentication uses 1Password, so configured host exceptions are expected. A clean rebase of the session's owned, non-shared feature branch onto main or origin/main is routine after inspecting the upstream, confirming no operation is in progress, and recording a recovery ref. Continue after understood conflicts are resolved, or abort to recover; do not ask again solely because this rewrites owned commits.

Worktrunk: wt list/status/config show/switch/merge/remove are routine within task scope and use host access for sibling worktrees. Preserve hook approvals, integration checks, and clean-worktree checks. Local branch cleanup uses git branch -d or guarded wt cleanup; forced cleanup is manual.

Git writes: task-authorized normal pushes to a verified non-protected branch on the intended remote are routine and should pass automatic review without another user confirmation. Resolve the actual destination, including refspecs and push configuration; do not infer protection from a branch name. Shared/protected targets need explicit task or repository authority, including main in trunk workflows. Guarded merges follow repository policy. Force-with-lease needs review and is limited to an owned feature branch. Publication and release changes have separate, stricter gates.

Notes vault: use notesmd-cli with --vault "$OBSIDIAN_DEFAULT_VAULT" for girlOS from any project. Requested individual note edits, moves, named deletions, frontmatter changes, and task status/date changes are routine. Capture only when requested; preserve identity and surrounding content.

Vault task sync: an explicit sync authorizes resolved changes to the named tasks and the org/_inbox/Task Sync record. Evaluate the complete change set; unrelated changes, ambiguous matches, mass deletion, and broad reorganization need review.

Reminders: reads and task-authorized individual add/update/complete/flag calls, including moves between established lists, are routine. rem runs on the host because EventKit is unreachable inside the sandbox. Deletion, imports/exports, and list administration reach review; assess multi-ID calls and loops as batches.

External skills: gh skill install/add/update/search/list/preview is routine within task scope, including user scope in the shared agent hub. Review unfamiliar sources and forced replacement; use gh skill instead of package-runner skills installers.

Tool upgrades: uv tool upgrade, mise up/upgrade, and other configured package-manager upgrades are routine. Keep pins, release-age cooldowns, signature/checksum checks, and native trust controls intact.

Project tasks: inspect mise run, deno task, task, and make invocations against project policy. A trusted, specifically authorized task is routine; an explicit release request authorizes the reviewed project release task with checks and confirmation gates intact.

Dotfiles inspection: chezmoi diff, cat, data, managed, doctor, verify, and any command run as `chezmoi --dry-run --no-pager <cmd>` are routine. They run on the host because chezmoi's state database sits outside the sandbox.
soft_deny: Force pushes: `--force-with-lease` on the session's own feature branch is the only permitted force form. Bare `--force` or `-f`, `--force-with-lease` on main or any shared or protected branch, and rewriting history the user did not ask to rewrite are blocked

Dotfiles deployment: editing files in the chezmoi source tree is routine, but a real `chezmoi apply`, `update`, or `init` rewrites the whole home directory, including exact_ directories, run scripts, and the shell config, and a half-finished workstream in the source tree can break the machine. Approve one only when the user's own message explicitly asked to apply after the changes; a request to edit dotfiles, and an agent's wish to verify its work, do not count. A sandboxed chezmoi command failing on its state database is never grounds to bypass the sandbox into a real apply; the dry run is the verification. Editing deployed user configs under ~ directly is blocked

Trust and permission surfaces: never edit trustfiles, allowlists, permission or sandbox settings, or build-script and postinstall approvals (agent permissions and sandbox config, mise trust, direnv allow, cargo/npm script trust, MCP or plugin trust state) to unblock work — surface the block and let the user decide. Change these only on a direct explicit ask to change that surface itself, never as a step toward another goal

Vault administration and batches: vault creation/removal, registration, and default-vault changes are manual-only. Review imports/exports, mass deletion, and broad restructuring as complete change sets, including loops of individual commands. Incidental capture does not authorize rematter or unrelated edits.
Fish universal variables: never create them (`set -U` / `set -Ux`); export with `set -gx` in the dotfiles repo instead

Task scope: an executable or trusted repository does not authorize every task. Review unknown task-runner commands and their effects; project-specific authority can approve the named task without changing global permission settings.
Publication: do not invoke raw package publishing, GitHub release mutation, or release workflow dispatch to bypass the reviewed project release task. Run that task only on explicit request.

Git cleanup and recovery: block remote ref deletion, mirror pushes, forced local branch/worktree deletion, and bypassing Worktrunk hooks or approvals. Rebase only owned work with a preserved starting state; never skip unresolved commits or discard unpreserved changes.
environment: **Organization**: Lightdash (@lightdash) for work; Supermodel Labs (@supermodellabs) for open-source side projects; personal work under @gwenwindflower
**Cloud provider(s)**: GCP for work, for personal projects Cloudflare + Fly.io + Railway serverless platforms are preferred depending on complexity and needs

**Agent sandboxes**: exe.dev for longer-running project sandboxes, Fly.io Sprites when running many shorter-running and/or frequently checkpointed sandboxes are better, microsandbox (msb) CLI for local sandboxes that are more contained than the default agent harness sandboxing permissions

**Repository visibility**: verify the intended repository and destination before publishing. Ordinary source pushes follow the task and repo workflow; package publication and releases use the reviewed project pipeline.

**Secrets management**: 1Password. The user's terminal commits are SSH-signed through it; agent sessions receive a hook-provided, session-scoped unsigned identity instead. Never edit global signing config or pass `--gpg-sign`, and never run `op`

**Default / protected branches**: `main` unless the repo says otherwise. Trunk-based development with linear history: rebase onto main, never merge with a merge commit, never force-push main or a shared branch
**CI/CD**: GitHub Actions based, use zizmor and pinact to keep these secure
**Network posture**: sandboxed shell egress is limited to the allowlisted domains and `WebFetch` has its own domain list; an unlisted host prompts and is never routed around

**Source control**: the repository the session started in and its configured remotes only; `gh` is the expected tool for GitHub work beyond core git, read before write, and `gh auth token` must never be run

**Sensitive data**: never expose credentials or commit unrelated personal data. Confidential project material follows repository-local policy; private visibility alone grants no additional task authority.

**Environment naming**: `prod` is production, `staging` is a long-lived staging environment, and `dev` is a development environment, each matched as a whole word or hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited name segment (`prod-db` matches, `producer` does not). Projects the user does not control may spell them `production` and `development`. Long-lived environments are rare by preference; short-lived per-PR or CI-gated environments are the norm, and any exception is flagged in the project itself

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, container, or resource whose name matches `prod` or `production` under the environment naming rule. `staging` is a shared environment and warrants care, not a block
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources, and anything whose name or tag matches `prod` or `production`
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development — spec- and test-driven work on developer tooling (Rust/Go/TypeScript/Python CLIs and TUIs), dotfiles managed with chezmoi, and docs/prose editing
**Trusted repo**: the repository the session is working in and its configured remotes. Inspect changed destinations and apply repository-local data and publication policy.

**Personal CLIs**: `herdr`, `wt`, `chezmoi`, `linear-cli`, `agent-browser`, `agentsview`, `notesmd-cli`, `rclone`, `mise`, `uv`, `deno`, `mint`, and `rip`/`fd`/`rg`/`bat`/`lsd`/`sd` as the preferred modern replacements
